payload.markdown: Unlike functions, methods must be declared in the body of a class. They can also accept a number of qualifiers, including a visibility keyword. Like properties, methods can be declared public, protected, or private. By declaring a method public, you ensure that it can be invoked from outside of the current object. If you omit the visibility keyword in your method declaration, the method will be declared public implicitly. It is considered good practice, however, to declare visibility explicitly for all methods (I will return to method modifiers later in the chapter).

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Functions: Reusable blocks of code that take arguments and return values.
PSR-1/12/4: PHP standards for coding style, file structure and autoloading.
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Variables: Named storage for a value; PHP infers the type from what you assign.
Visibility & Encapsulation: public, protected and private control who may read or write a member.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Arrow Functions: fn() => expressions: closures with automatic by-value capture.

8146.title: Working with Methods
8146.code:
<?php
class ShopProduct
{
    public $title = "default product";
    public $producerMainName = "main name";
    public $producerFirstName = "first name";
    public $price = 0;

    public function getProducer()
    {
        return $this->producerFirstName . " "
            . $this->producerMainName;
    }
}
